To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
macrophages are important to the healing of wounds in mice, and that the ability of macrophages to heal wounds is impaired with age.

the impaired wound healing observed in aged animals can be attributed to a defect in the macrophage response to the wound and that local injection of exogenous macrophages can partially correct the defect.

macrophage therapy can accelerate healing of experimentally induced cuta- neous wounds of old mice to levels comparable to those of young animals, and that this acceleration is greater when macrophages obtained from young as oppo- site to old donors are used.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the mechanisms underlying the age-associated changes in the function of macrophages and other cells involved in the immune response and in the inflammatory response, and their relationship to the age-associated changes of the immune system.
the role of macrophages in wound repair.
the study of the mechanisms of aging at the cellular level.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the macrophage is the cell of the immune system that has the most important effect on wound repair and that the macrophages are the most important cells in wound repair.
the macrophage is an important cellular component in wound repair, and that its functional capacity is impaired in senescence.
macrophage therapy is effective in promoting wound healing in aged mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
macrophages can be used as a tool for accelerating wound repair in old animals.
the age-related decline in wound repair is due to a defect in the macrophage response to wounding.
we have shown that the impaired wound healing in old animals is caused by a deficiency in the macrophage response to injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can promote healing in old mice by giving them young macrophages.
macrophages can be used as a tool to promote wound repair in the aged.
the age-related defect in wound healing is not due to a defect in fibroblasts but rather in macrophages.
